topic.title: Linux Administration
topic.description: Processes, services, logs, disks, files and permissions on Linux servers

commands.name: ps
commands.description: Prints a one-time snapshot of processes. BSD-style options (aux) and standard options (-ef, -o) can select and format columns.

flags.description: BSD style: processes of all users that have a terminal.
BSD style: user-oriented format with %CPU, %MEM, VSZ and RSS.
BSD style: include processes without a terminal (daemons).
Sort by a column; prefix with - for descending.

examples.title: All processes with resource usage
examples.scenario: The server is slow. List every process with user, CPU and memory usage.
examples.explanation: a: all users, u: user-oriented columns, x: include daemons without a terminal.
examples.output:
USER       PID %CPU %MEM    VSZ   RSS TTY  STAT START TIME COMMAND
root         1  0.0  0.1 168000 12800 ?    Ss   09:01 0:02 /sbin/init
www-data  1421  2.3  0.5  88320 43120 ?    S    09:02 0:13 nginx: worker

output_notes.meaning: Resident memory in KiB actually held in RAM.
output_notes.anomaly: Steady growth over hours: likely leak.

output_notes.meaning: Process state: R running, S sleeping, D uninterruptible I/O wait, Z zombie.
output_notes.anomaly: Many D or Z states.

examples.title: Top memory consumers
examples.scenario: Find which processes use the most memory, largest first.
examples.explanation: --sort=-%mem orders by memory descending; head keeps the first 10 lines.
examples.output:
USER   PID  %CPU %MEM    VSZ     RSS TTY STAT START TIME COMMAND
app   3100  12.4 61.2 6.1G   4.8G   ?   Sl   08:00 41:22 java -jar api.jar
postgres 912 1.1 8.3 1.2G 650M  ?   Ss   Nov19 3:10 postgres: checkpointer

output_notes.meaning: Share of physical RAM used by the java process.
output_notes.normal: Within the memory budget planned for the service.
output_notes.anomaly: Above ~50% for one process on a shared host: OOM risk for everything else.

output_notes.meaning: Sleeping (S) and multi-threaded (l).

examples.title: Custom columns for one PID
examples.scenario: Show PID, parent PID, state, CPU, memory and command line for process 3100.
examples.explanation: -o picks the columns, -p selects the process.
examples.output:
PID  PPID STAT %CPU %MEM COMMAND
 3100     1 Dl    0.3 61.2 java -jar api.jar

output_notes.meaning: D: uninterruptible sleep, waiting on I/O; l: multi-threaded.
output_notes.anomaly: Persistent D: blocked on disk or NFS; it will not die even with KILL.

output_notes.meaning: Parent process; 1 means systemd adopted or started it.

use_cases.situation: A nightly job never finished and now several copies run in parallel; ps shows their start times.

pitfalls: %CPU is averaged over the process lifetime, not the current instant; use top for live usage.

flags.description: State, main PID, recent log lines of a unit.

Start the unit at boot; --now also starts it immediately.

commands.name: df
commands.description: Reports used and available space and inodes for mounted filesystems.

examples.scenario: Writes are failing. Check free space on every mounted filesystem.
examples.output:
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/vda1        50G   48G  2.0G  97% /
/dev/vdb1       200G   61G  139G  31% /data

output_notes.meaning: Share of blocks in use.
output_notes.anomaly: > 90%: writes and logs will soon fail.

examples.title: Inode exhaustion
examples.scenario: Disk shows free space but files cannot be created. Check inode usage.
examples.explanation: Millions of tiny files can exhaust inodes while blocks are still free.
examples.output:
Filesystem      Inodes   IUsed  IFree IUse% Mounted on
/dev/vda1      3276800 3276800      0  100% /

output_notes.meaning: Share of inodes in use.
output_notes.anomaly: 100%: no new files can be created even with free blocks.

examples.title: Filesystem types
examples.scenario: List mounts with their filesystem type in human-readable sizes.
examples.output:
Filesystem     Type   Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/vda1      ext4    50G   31G   17G  65% /
tmpfs          tmpfs  3.9G  1.2M  3.9G   1% /run

output_notes.meaning: RAM-backed filesystem; its contents vanish on reboot and use memory.
output_notes.anomaly: Large usage in tmpfs consumes RAM.

procedures.title: Reproduce the stopped (T) process state
procedures.context: You want to see what a paused process looks like without touching production services.

steps.interpretation: Job 1 with PID 4242 runs in the background.

steps.purpose: Pause it ($! is the last background PID)

T means stopped by a signal.
KILL ends even a stopped process; TERM would stay pending until the process is continued.
